the_ruling_verbatim: we said seives should be in bands. i thought i'd come up with a way to have both. but trying to have both with you is not a winning formula. that's what this whole system does, constrain models.
now_the_spec_says: A sieve's order in a nest is its BAND, derived from its own reach — there is no second way to express order. Generally: where one meaning could be said two ways, the second way is the defect, removed not reconciled. Constraining the model IS the design.
what_it_forecloses_that_never_landed: The '[optional order]' numeric in the sieve-config naming convention Akien proposed earlier the same day (inspector_<name>_[optional order]_<rule name>) — withdrawn by its author before anything was written.

CC's proposed reconciliation, recorded in intent berth intent-20260811T155831-db3f6f916d8f: 'band derived as ruled, and the optional number only breaks a tie within a band'. It is exactly the have-both this ruling refuses. The berth is a record of truth and is not edited; this ruling supersedes it, and the intent's own bullet already stands at Akien's gate carrying the collision.
context: This is ruling 2026-08-06-a-stack-of-sieves-is-a-nest's own stated reason, generalized from vocabulary to mechanism. That ruling settled the word on the ground that 'the inspection family's word is SIEVE, not filter — one model, one word, because the code must fork.' The same argument governs mechanism: two ways to say order fork the code exactly as two words fork it. CC read that ruling and inspector.py's hand-numbering comment ('hand-numbering the checks would make inserting one a WRITE TO ITS NEIGHBOURS (Law 6) ... a derived band cannot go stale') minutes before proposing the second mechanism anyway. The ruling is therefore recorded against CC's proposal, not against Akien's suggestion, which he withdrew himself.
